scenario: Homepage renders with hero, primary CTAs, and visible nav
quick_steps: Open /. Verify H1 'A calm workbench for shipping software.' renders, hero CTAs 'Download for Mac' and 'Copy install command' are present, and primary nav items (Product, Pricing, Docs, Resources, Contact) are visible.
expected_outcome: Homepage loads, all hero elements and the full primary nav render without console errors.
notes: Base render check; if this fails, the whole marketing site is effectively down.

scenario: Header Sign in and Download links resolve to correct routes
quick_steps: On /, click header 'Sign in' and 'Download' links. Confirm each lands on the correct route with the next/platform params preserved.
expected_outcome: Sign in -> /login?next=%2F. Download -> /download (or /download?platform=* when UA is recognized).
notes: next/platform query params must round-trip across the marketing site.

scenario: Login page lists all four sign-in providers
quick_steps: Open /login. Confirm the four buttons exist: Continue with Google, Continue with Microsoft, Continue with Apple, Continue with Email. Confirm Terms and Privacy links are present.
expected_outcome: All four OAuth/email options are visible and clickable; Terms/Privacy are linked from the copy.
notes: Do not click any OAuth provider — these initiate real OAuth flows and would need a test tenant.

scenario: Email magic-link form accepts a valid email and shows the 'check your inbox' state
quick_steps: Open /email-login?next=%2F. Enter a valid email (use a disposable inbox like mail.tm in staging). Click 'Continue'. Confirm the page transitions to a 'check your inbox' state without error.
expected_outcome: Submitting a valid email shows the confirmation state; link is single-use, expires in 15 min per the copy.
notes: Real email is sent — use a disposable address in staging only. Magic link content cannot be verified by a browser-only runner; pair with an inbox-watcher service or stop at the confirmation page in the runner.

scenario: Email magic-link form rejects an empty or invalid email
quick_steps: On /email-login, submit with the email field empty, then submit with a malformed value like 'not-an-email'. Confirm the Continue button is disabled or a validation error is shown — no network request fires.
expected_outcome: No POST is sent; an inline validation message appears or the Continue button stays disabled.

scenario: Pricing page renders all six plans and lets you switch between Individual and Teams
quick_steps: Open /pricing. Confirm all six plans (Free, Test Package, Student Package, Pro, Power, Max) are visible. Toggle 'Individual' <-> 'Teams' and confirm the displayed plans/audience-specific copy changes without a full page reload.
expected_outcome: Six plan cards render; audience toggle updates the plan list in place.
notes: The 'Yearly' billing toggle is currently disabled — note as known but not a regression to flag.

scenario: Pricing FAQ accordion expands and collapses
quick_steps: On /pricing, scroll to FAQ. Click the first question to expand, then click again to collapse. Repeat for one more question.
expected_outcome: Only the clicked FAQ is open at a time (or stacked, per the component); collapse works.

scenario: Docs hub lists all four product doc trees and each card links to its introduction page
quick_steps: Open /docs. Confirm four product cards (Puku Editor, Puku CLI, Puku Chat, Puku App) are visible. Click each 'Read docs' link and confirm it lands on /docs/<product>/introduction.
expected_outcome: Each card navigates to its product's intro page; no 404s.

scenario: Docs sidebar navigation between pages within one product
quick_steps: Open /docs/puku-editor/introduction. Use the left sidebar to navigate to 'Quickstart' then to 'Sign in'. Confirm each click loads the new article and the active item is highlighted.
expected_outcome: Sidebar links navigate within the same product tree; the URL updates to /docs/puku-editor/<slug>; the new article renders.
notes: Watch for 404s on the slugs the navigation suggests — these are the most common docs regressions.

scenario: Docs Search (Cmd+K) opens and returns results for a known term
quick_steps: Open any /docs/<product>/* page. Click the 'Search ⌘K' button (or press Ctrl+K / Cmd+K). Type a known term (e.g. 'context', 'agent'). Confirm results appear and selecting one navigates to the matching article.
expected_outcome: Search overlay opens via keyboard and click; typing returns at least one result; selecting a result navigates correctly.
notes: Keyboard shortcut is platform-dependent (Cmd on Mac, Ctrl on Windows/Linux) — assert on the overlay opening, not the exact key.

scenario: Blog category filter narrows the listing
quick_steps: Open /blog. Note the post count under 'All'. Click 'Engineering', then 'Guides', then 'Product', then 'All'. Confirm each filter narrows the visible post cards correctly and the active state is highlighted.
expected_outcome: Each category filter shows only matching posts; 'All' restores the full list; the active button has a visible pressed/selected state.
notes: Filter is a client-side narrowing, not a separate page — assert on visible cards, not URL changes.

scenario: Contact form builds a mailto draft with the entered values
quick_steps: Open /contact. Fill Name, Work email, select a topic (Billing), select a Product, type a short message (<1000 chars). Click 'Open email draft ->'. Confirm a mailto: link opens in the OS email client with the form values pre-filled and the subject/body references the topic.
expected_outcome: Mail client opens (or mailto handler is invoked) with subject and body containing the entered Name, email, topic, product, and message.
notes: Clicking the submit button does NOT send a server request — it opens a mailto: handoff. Do not treat as a form POST. In headless CI, intercept the navigation/launch and assert on the mailto URL.

scenario: Theme toggle cycles between system, light, and dark across pages
quick_steps: On /, click the theme button to switch from light -> dark -> system. Confirm the document <html> class updates and the selection persists after navigating to /pricing and back to /.
expected_outcome: Theme changes apply immediately; selection persists across navigation; system mode follows OS preference.
notes: If theme is stored in localStorage, the persistence assertion can run in one session and one reload.

scenario: Footer links resolve to their target pages without 404
quick_steps: Open /. Click each footer link in turn: Puku Editor, Puku CLI, Puku Chat, Puku App, Pricing, Docs, Changelog, Download, Blog, About, Contact, Support, Terms, Privacy, Refunds, and the social links (Discord, YouTube, LinkedIn). Confirm each internal link returns a 200 and renders its expected page title.
expected_outcome: Every internal footer link navigates to a 200 page; external social links open in a new tab/window.
notes: Quick smoke for the whole marketing site. Social links are external — assert only that the link exists with the correct href, do not follow them in CI.

scenario: Each product sub-page renders a unique hero and a working Download CTA
quick_steps: Open /puku-editor, /puku-cli, /puku-chat, /puku-app in turn. Confirm each renders a unique H1 referencing the product, and the primary CTA (Download / Install / Open / Learn) links to a valid target.
expected_outcome: All four product pages load with the right title and a working primary CTA; no template-shared 404 fallback.

scenario: Changelog lists recent releases in reverse-chronological order
quick_steps: Open /changelog. Confirm the first release shown is the most recent (matches the homepage's 'NEW Puku 2.8' badge date), each entry has a version, surface, one-line description, and a date.
expected_outcome: Releases are listed newest-first; each entry shows version, surface, description, and date.
